subject: Copywriting
title: The Decoy Effect
description: Learn The Decoy Effect in one minute.

hook.text: The Economist offered: web-only $59, print $125, web+print $125. Nobody picked print alone. It existed to sell both.

buildup.text: Dan Ariely tested this. Without the decoy, 68% chose web-only. With it, 84% chose the combo.

discovery.text: The decoy makes the target option look irrationally good. It's not compared to all choices, just the decoy.

twist.text: Movie popcorn uses the same trick. Small $3, medium $6.50, large $7. The medium makes the large look obvious.

climax.text: SaaS pricing pages almost always have three tiers. The middle one usually exists to push you to the top.

punchline.text: The middle option exists to sell the expensive one.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of a decoy option in pricing?
options: To make the target option look like better value

details.summary: The decoy effect uses a strategically inferior option to make a target option look better. When Apple offers 64GB, 128GB, and 256GB iPhones, the middle option often exists primarily to make the 256GB feel like a smart upgrade. Decoys shape choice without the buyer realizing it.
details.whyItMatters: The decoy effect is one of pricing psychology's most elegant tools. Understanding it helps copywriters design pricing pages that steer customers toward preferred options while maintaining the feeling of free choice.
takeaways: A decoy option makes the target option appear more attractive by comparison
Three-tier pricing often uses the middle tier as a decoy
The decoy must be clearly inferior to the target but similar enough to invite comparison

faq.question: How do you set up a decoy in pricing?
faq.answer: Create three options where the middle tier is priced close to the premium tier but offers significantly less. The small price gap between middle and premium makes the premium feel like a no-brainer. The cheap option exists for price-sensitive buyers; the middle exists to sell the top tier.

faq.question: Does the decoy effect work online?
faq.answer: Extremely well. SaaS pricing pages almost universally use three tiers with a highlighted 'most popular' option. The visual highlighting combines the decoy effect with social proof, and the side-by-side comparison makes the contrast immediately obvious.
